any-professional.blurb: A normal week on the job — until three people need different things by Friday.

moments.text: It is 9:40am. your manager drops a vague request about the team's weekly report on you and calls it urgent.

options.text: Ask what decision the request feeds and who else needs it.
options.feedback: That is the professional move: slow enough to be right, fast enough to matter.

options.text: Start on the obvious version and check in later.
options.feedback: It buys time, but someone downstream pays for it.

options.text: Guess what they mean and start building.
options.feedback: Fast, but you will be back here tomorrow.

moments.text: You open the shared workspace and the numbers do not match what your manager quoted in the meeting.

options.text: Recheck the source before repeating the number.
options.feedback: Excellent. You protected the relationship and the outcome at the same time.

options.text: Note the mismatch and carry on with a caveat.
options.feedback: Not wrong, not finished. The real question is still open.

options.text: Use the number that looks more credible.
options.feedback: The shortcut is now someone else's incident.

moments.text: You find the real problem — and it is bigger than the request.

options.text: Scope the bigger issue, then agree what is in this pass.
options.feedback: Strong. You treated the cause, not the symptom.

options.feedback: Reasonable, but the underlying issue is still there.

options.text: Stick to the original request.
options.feedback: This buys time and spends trust.
